newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta, Ontario to lead Canada growth, study says.
newsitem.headline: Alberta, Ontario to lead Canada growth, study says.

text.p: Canada's economic growth will double in 1997, and the strongest growth will occur in Alberta and Ontario, said a study released on Thursday by a Canadian economic research institute.
The Conference Board of Canada predicted in its spring provincial outlook that Canada's real gross domestic product (GDP) will grow 2.9 percent in 1997 and 2.7 percent in 1998.
Alberta will grow the fastest this year at 3.8 percent, followed by slower growth of 2.8 percent in 1998, the board said.
Ontario's economy will post growth of 3.6 percent in 1997 and 3.1 percent next year, the board added.

"Stronger consumer spending and continued export gains will drive economic activity in Ontario as consumers benefit from recent declines in personal income tax rates," said Paul Darby, the board's director of economic services.
"Alberta will see rapid expansion thanks to excellent conditions in the oil and gas industry," Darby said.
The study indicated that Prince Edward Island, the smallest of Canada's Atlantic provinces, would grow the least at 0.1 percent in 1997 and 1.7 percent in 1998.
